subject: business
summary: Plain text questions (define a term, explain two benefits) read clearly and the case-study stems are complete. Anything with a table or chart is broken: the unemployment table shows raw pipe characters and the break-even chart is replaced by a string of loose axis numbers, with no picture inline. The scheme section is the weakest part: the 'What the scheme printed' tick list regularly contains rows that are not answers at all (headers, annotation legends, answers to a different question, a line broken in two), every row carries the full-question mark badge, and the mark grid rows are labelled only 'Component 1 / Component 2'. Every card attaches a full uncropped exam page; 6 of 12 open on a different question. The layout itself is tidy on both phone and desktop, but schemes with tick list plus grid run to two or three phone screens.

issues.title: Junk rows in the 'What the scheme printed' tick list
issues.detail: The tick list includes text that is not a marking point. Card 3: 'Calculations:', 'Break Even Point =', 'Chart:' (twice), 'The table below contains information about annotations used for marking throughout the exam paper', 'Annotation Use', 'Correct element (n marks) No marks awarded. Answer incorrect or insufficient. Page seen by examiner...', 'Evaluation', 'EVAL' - the examiner annotation legend has been pasted in as tickable answers. Card 11: a row reading 'Question Possible Responses Max. Mark' (a table header). Card 10: one answer is split across two rows, 'Brings business into Abbeyglen - customers/ suppliers of Glentronic' then a separate tick box 'Pharmaceuticals'. Card 7: rows start with a stray bullet character.
issues.suggested_fix: Strip headers, legends and labels with no content; rejoin wrapped lines; for card 3 show the three calculations as three clean lines (BEP = 40,000/10 = 4,000 units, etc.) and, since the answer is a chart, show a crop of the official break-even chart.

issues.title: Scheme lists answers to a different question
issues.detail: Card 2 (Q3, reasons to become an entrepreneur) starts its tick list with 'Social Needs', 'Security/Safety Needs' and 'Physiological/Physical Needs 3 Three reasons why a person would consider becoming an entrepreneur:'. Those are the answers to Q2 (Maslow's hierarchy) from the same scheme page, with Q3's own heading glued on the end. A student could tick 'Social Needs' as a reason to be an entrepreneur.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the three Q2 rows and the pasted heading; start the list at 'Own boss / self-employed / independent / own decisions'.

issues.title: Table and chart flattened into raw text
issues.detail: Card 1 prints the data table as '| November 2007 | May 2008 | November 2008 | May 2009' and 'Total persons on the Live Register | 150,000 | 200,000 | 250,000 | 400,000' with literal pipe characters, in the large serif question face. Card 4 replaces the break-even chart with '(Chart: TR TC € ’000s 700 600 500 400 300 200 100 Costs & Revenues FC 5 10 15 Output in units ’000s; the TR, TC and FC lines are drawn on the printed grid.)' - the student cannot read the profit off that, and the only underlined 'question' is the caption 'Break-even chart'. Neither card shows the figure inline.
issues.suggested_fix: Card 1: render a real two-row table. Card 4: show a crop of the printed break-even chart inline (the question cannot be answered without it) and make '(ii) The Profit at Forecast Sales (15,000 units) in euros' the underlined ask.

issues.title: Attached page opens on a different question
issues.detail: The 'Read question paper' attachment is the whole uncropped page and the reader opens at its top. Card 1 (Q3) shows the whole of Q2 (Wholefood Farm Products, parts A-E), Q3 only begins at the bottom edge. Card 2 (Q3) shows Q1 (PAYE/PRSI/USC) and Q2 (Maslow pyramid). Card 4 (Q10) shows Q8 and Q9, the chart is cut off at the bottom. Card 5 (Q7) shows Q4 true/false table, Q5 and Q6; Q7 is not visible. Card 6 (Q10) shows all of Q9. Card 7 (Q3) shows all of Q2 (LPT). The attachment is titled with the right question number, so it looks like a mistake.
issues.suggested_fix: Crop to the card's own question, or drop the attachment where the full question is already in the text (cards 2, 5, 6, 7). For cards 1 and 4 crop to the table/chart and show it inline.

issues.title: Attached page shows all sibling parts
issues.detail: Where the page is the right question it shows every other part with marks: card 3 shows Q8(A) and (B) with (C) off-screen; card 8 shows (A), (B); cards 9, 10, 11, 12 show parts A to E around the target.
issues.suggested_fix: Crop to the stimulus box plus the one part asked.

issues.title: Mark badges and grid labels are confusing
issues.detail: Every row in the tick list carries the same badge, and it is the whole-question or whole-item figure, not what that row is worth: card 2 shows '10m' on each of 11 reasons (each is worth 4, 3 or 3), card 8 '6m' on each heading (worth 3), card 7 '10m', card 3 '13M THEN 12M' above every row. The grid underneath then asks for the marks again, with rows labelled only 'Component 1' / 'Component 2' (cards 4, 5, 6, 9, 10, 11, 12) or 'Explain' twice (card 7), so the student cannot tell which is the statement and which is the development/example. The sentence 'A claimed response takes the full marks of the next response below; use its buttons for part marks.' is hard to follow. Card 4 has both a 2m tick and a 0/2 grid for one answer.
issues.suggested_fix: Drop the per-row badge or show the real per-point value; label grid rows by what earns the marks ('Statement 3' / 'Example 2', 'Name 4' / 'Explain 3' / 'Develop 3'); for a single-figure answer show only the tick.

issues.title: Scheme text run together without punctuation
issues.detail: Card 12 prints the scheme's bullet points as one unpunctuated string: 'Usually once off No requirement to pay back Must meet conditions what grant is for Available from LEO, Enterprise Ireland, IDA, EU'; 'Must have facility on current account Can take out more money than actually in your account Agreed limit Interest paid...'. Card 6 puts both definitions in one tick box marked 5m, the second half ('whereas Import substitution refers to...') in small grey text as if it were a note. Card 1's summary line 'Title 2 and each of the four bars 2.' and card 3's 'X axis 1, Y axis 1, title 1, FC line 2, TC and TR lines 4 each' are terse examiner shorthand.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep the scheme's bullets as bullets under each heading; split card 6 into two tick boxes, one per term; write mark summaries as a sentence ('Title: 2 marks. Each of the four bars: 2 marks.').

issues.title: Part labels and lost underlining in the question
issues.detail: Part labels are left in front of the ask: '(A) (i) Draw a bar chart' (card 1), '(i) List two headings' (card 8), '(C) Explain two possible benefits' (card 10), '(ii) Explain two of the three sources' (card 12), '(ii) The Profit at Forecast Sales' (card 4). Card 9 asks 'Explain two of the underlined terms' but the terms (partnership, private company limited by shares, diversifying) are not underlined; worse, the app's own orange highlight underlines 'name. Up until 2019 it operated', which is not one of them. Card 2 ends on a dangling colon.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove part labels (the header already gives the reference); underline or bold the three terms in card 9 and put the orange highlight on the instruction line; trim the trailing colon.

issues.title: Long scheme on the phone
issues.detail: Tick list plus full grid plus boilerplate makes the revealed card two to three phone screens tall (card 3 runs to three columns; cards 7, 10, 11 to two and a half). The grade buttons end up far below the question. Card 3's grid rows wrap so the label sits above its buttons for some rows and beside them for others.
issues.suggested_fix: Collapse the sample-answer list behind a toggle once the grid is in view, or merge tick and grid into one control per point.

good_examples.why: Stem and ask are clear, scheme lists seven clean headings and a simple 0/3/6 total.
Scheme gives each of the three terms as a titled box with its explanation; easy to check an answer against (question side has the underline fault).
One-line question, one-line model answer, fits a single phone screen.
